summary: Milestone execution completed 3 experiments in 1.7 minutes; 2 were compute-bound. Recovered cold entrance-bank sufficiency audit was the longest listed task at 1.74 minutes, but the supplied data do not identify why it took longest.
bottlenecks_identified: Elapsed time was concentrated in Recovered cold entrance-bank sufficiency audit, but no phase timings are available to explain the concentration.
Task-correlated accelerator telemetry is absent, so the milestone-close idle GPU snapshot cannot establish compute-window utilization efficiency.
Model-count, concurrency, and runner-dispatch evidence are absent, so DualGPURunner eligibility and use cannot be assessed.
improvements_suggested: Record per-experiment phase timestamps so setup, loading, inference, validation, and artifact-writing costs can be separated.
Capture experiment-correlated GPU utilization samples for compute-bound task windows rather than relying on a milestone-close snapshot.
Emit launch receipts containing concurrent model count and runner choice, and use DualGPURunner when at least two models are loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add per-experiment phase timing to locate the cost inside the longest compute-bound task.
Add task-window GPU telemetry keyed to each compute-bound experiment.
Record model concurrency and runner dispatch at launch so eligible parallel workloads can be audited.
meta_reflection: The supplied data rank elapsed time but do not support a causal explanation, a compute-window utilization judgment, or a DualGPURunner compliance finding. The next retrospective would be more actionable with task-aligned phase, GPU, and dispatch records.
